title: GOATED Usage Log Entry
description: One line of the usage log the enforcement core appends to (Ticket 082): JSON Lines, one entry per line, oldest first. Every adapter writes through the core, so a session in any harness leaves the same entries. An entry holds what the skill-usage mod stores and nothing more: no prompt text, hold text, file content, or project path. The log lives where its caller says (`--usage-log`, `GOATED_USAGE_LOG`; `off` keeps none). The core's command keeps none unless one is named; the Claude Code adapter's default is a per-user folder, never a project's: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\goated\usage-log.jsonl` on Windows (else the per-user temp folder's `goated`), else `$XDG_STATE_HOME/goated/usage-log.jsonl`, else `~/.local/state/goated/usage-log.jsonl`. The folder is the user's alone. Its project keys and file digests are salted with `usage-log-salt` beside it. Writers append each event's lines in one write under a lock on the log, `usage-log.jsonl.lock`. Readers refuse a log with an entry of another version, not guessing at it, and pass over, counting them, lines that are no entry: not JSON, not an object, or missing a field its type needs. `adapters/core/goated_usage_report.py` summarises it. The log is never trimmed.

log.description: The log's version: a whole number every change of an entry's meaning bumps. Version 2 (round 6, R15) adds `notice` entries and a hold's `file_class`; a version 1 entry means the same in version 2, so readers take both.

t.description: When the core wrote the entry, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

adapter.description: The adapter's short name, such as `claude-code`, or what a harness calling the command sets in `GOATED_CORE_ADAPTER` (`core` by default).

session.description: The session id the adapter gave the core.

project.description: The project's key: the first ten hex digits of the SHA-256 digest of the log's salt and the project folder's path, the folder being its repository's root (the main working tree's, for a worktree). The key does not reveal the path. Null when the adapter named no folder.

agent.description: The subagent acting, absent for the main agent.

prompt.description: A typed prompt opened a turn. `named`: the installed skills its text names, backticked, slashed, or as a whole word; the text itself is not kept.

override.description: The overrides the core recorded for the prompt just logged, each phrase as matched, lowercased (`skip routing`, `skip tdd`, `commit message`).

load.description: A skill loaded: a skill load call finished ok, or a person invoked it. `skill` is its bare name, a plugin namespace dropped. `cause`, judged in this order: `slash` (a person invoked it), `subagent` (a subagent chose it; `hold` when a hold asked that subagent), `named` (the turn's prompt named it), `hold` (a hold of the turn asked for it), `route` (it loaded after the router in the turn), `agent` (the agent chose it).

hold.description: A hold the core showed, as what it asks for, read from its text the way the skill-usage mod reads it; the text is not kept. `named`: the skills it backticks alone or offers as a skip line, in order (the router for `router-first`; none for `route-line`, which asks for a route line). `skip_only`: those it offers only as a skip line, which no load answers. `refs`: the references a `design` or `design-reads` hold (by file name) or a `reference-reads` hold (by path under the skill) asks to read. `items`: a closeout's items, each with the skill its line names. `brief_added`: the orientation skill a pipeline hold asks for because the session started from a brief. `stop`: it held a turn's end, not a call. `file_class` (version 2): the class of the file the held call writes, a file write's file or the first file a shell command names as written, never its path: `test` (by its place in the project), `code`, `docs`, `configuration`, or `other`; absent for a call that names no file it writes, such as a commit, a spawn, or a turn's end.

outcome.description: What became of the main agent's hold of `gate`, as the core settles it for its friction count: `answered` (its asks were met, or its gate let the action through), `declined` (a skip line named its skill; never a strict hold), `stood_down` (the next typed prompt's override covered it), `unanswered` (still open at the next typed prompt). One outcome per gate and turn, however often the gate held in it. The skill-usage mod settles holds itself and does not read these.

skip.description: A valid `goated-skip:` line in reply text or a call's line text. `reason`: each path in a word, its wrapping quotes, backticks, brackets and trailing punctuation kept, masked as `<path>` (a path starts with a drive, a slash, or `~/`, holds a backslash or `://`, or holds a slash and either a second one or a file extension at its end; `and/or` stays), then cut to 160 characters, its last an ellipsis.

route.description: The winning `goated-route:` line of one reply text or one call's line text.

ref.description: A file read or shell command reached an installed skill's supporting file: `file` is its path within the skill (`references/test-design.md`). A folder named `skills` whose subfolder is no installed skill, such as a project's own, is never logged. `read_tool`: by a file read, not a command; `partial`: that read had a range, so it answers no hold.

skill_read.description: A main-agent file read or shell command reached into these installed skills' folders (their SKILL.md or any file in them).

file_read.description: A main-agent file read finished ok. `file` is a digest of the path, never the path: the first 16 hex digits of the SHA-256 digest of the log's salt and the path in comparable form (slashes forward and lowercased for a Windows path, `.` and `..` collapsed), so distinct files can be counted but a guessed path cannot be checked without the salt. None is written when the salt cannot be read.

notice.description: Version 2: a notice the event carried, by its kind alone, never its text: a kind of the event model's notices, such as `reads_owed`, `skip_carried`, `route_continued`, `override_recorded`, `closeout_note`, `session_notice`, or `warning`. A warning that the log itself could not be written is not logged.

bare.description: `change`: a file write to a code file finished ok. `turn_end`: the core let the turn end as an answer. `compaction`: the context was compacted, so earlier loads no longer count.
